title: The end of the Buck and Bubbles era and $650 a week apiece
summary: Bubbles' pneumonia ended the arrangement; the pair moved around hotels and by their peak earned $650 apiece weekly with rising pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, I would always get the $250.00, you see. That was sufficient for me, because it was kind of -- the work was kind of steady, because as I say, Chuck and Chuckles was on the increase, from stopping so many shows, you see, and we became the Kennedy favorites, right after that, about a year and a half or so after that, and by the way, in the same city, Boston, Massachusetts. And we had played the Boston Conservatory of Music so many times, and that's why we were going into stardom, because there was an important height in show business at that time. Anyone who had played the Boston Conservatory of Music was considered, you know, a principal act.
But at this time were you performing alone or were you still with Buck and Bubbles?
No, we were with Chuck and Chuckles at this time.
So when did the Buck and Bubbles era end?
Well, that ended in 1936, I think. 1934. I beg your pardon.
Was there any particular reason why it ended?

Yeah, well, Mr. Bubbles, he got pneumonia, and then he recovered, but he had had a wisdom tooth out, and about a week later he contracted double pneumonia, you see, and he had a bout with it again. So he recovered that bout, see, and while he was sick he allowed us to appear in Connie's Inn, places like that, and live away from the apartment, his family and so forth.
Did you move into a place by yourselves?

Yes. We moved into the Woodside Hotel, and then from the Woodside Hotel we went to the Shore Hotel, and we went back down to the Belvedere Hotel. Then we went over to Mr. Nat Nazarra's new apartment and --
Was this the height of your career at this point?
Yes. We had -- look, we went to about --
the Bill Bojangles -- after the Kennedy Favorites -- we became the Favorites, that's when the height of our career really progressed.
And you were getting paid the most at this particular time that you had ever been paid.
Yes.
And you were ever to be paid.
Yes.
That was about $600.00 a week.
Uh-huh.
Apiece. That's what we got.
650 a week apiece.
It was about $1,300.00 that the Chuck and Chuckles act got.
You were being treated fairly, I would imagine, with the money?
Yes, we were. Uh-huh.
Were there any mis-communications or mis-happenings with the money, or producers, at that time?

No, no. There was always an increase. We always would get increases in pay. That's another way, they knew that the money was going -- we were getting popular. More in demand, as they said in show business.
